sections.h2: Where do I search Brevard County property records?
sections.html:
Start with the Official Records search run by the Brevard County Clerk of Court and Comptroller, which is the county recorder. The search lives on the clerk's Acclaim site, and it covers deeds, mortgages, liens and other recorded instruments.

The Acclaim landing page asks you to accept a disclaimer before you search. The county says it tried to keep the index accurate but gives no guarantee, and it tells users to try every spelling variation of a name. That advice matters in Brevard, where a name on a deed may differ from the name on a mortgage by a middle initial or a suffix.

Questions about the search system go to the clerk's phone line at (321) 637-2004, which is printed on the Acclaim page. The same page lists e-recording information, a property fraud alert link and notices about how a person can ask the clerk to hide protected information from the public website.

sections.h2: Which clerk offices serve Brevard County?
sections.html:
The clerk lists six offices on its fees page, so you can usually find one close to the part of the county where the house sits. The list below follows that page.

  • Viera, 2825 Judge Fran Jamieson Wy
  • Titusville, 400 South St, plus a Parkway Complex office at 700 S. Park Ave (Bldg. B)
  • Melbourne, 51 Nieman Ave
  • Palm Bay, 450 Cogan Dr SE, closed between 11:30 AM and 1:30 PM
  • Merritt Island, also closed between 11:30 AM and 1:30 PM

The Viera, Titusville, Melbourne and Parkway offices show 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The clerk's mailing address for records matters is P.O. Box 2767, Titusville, Florida 32781-2767. Check the clerk's site before you drive over, since hours shift around holidays and the office posts closure notices on its home page.

sections.h2: What does Florida law say the clerk records?
sections.html:
Under Florida law the circuit court clerk acts as county recorder and files every instrument that must or may be recorded in one general series called the Official Records. That series stays open for public inspection and copying, subject to the service charges the clerk sets under s. 28.24.

Recording protects a buyer. A conveyance, transfer or mortgage of real property, or a lease of one year or longer, does not hold up against creditors or later purchasers who had no notice unless it is recorded under Florida law. For a seller, that means a deed signed at a kitchen table is not finished until it reaches the clerk.

A deed also has a form rule. Florida requires a written conveyance of land to be signed with two subscribing witnesses, and the statute allows the witnessing to happen over audio-video technology (s. 689.01). Clerks apply these formalities when they accept an instrument for filing.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Brevard County?
sections.html:
The base charge is set by statute: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each further page of an instrument within the standard size, with other charges layered on top. The clerk's own fee page is the place to confirm the total for a specific document.

Recording charges listed in s. 28.24(13), Florida Statutes

Same fund, each additional page$0.50
Added technology charge, per page$4

Brevard's fees page, as it opened, did not print a fee schedule, so ask the clerk to quote the exact total before you send a document in.

sections.h2: What documentary stamp tax applies to a Brevard deed?
sections.html:
Brevard County follows the statewide rate of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration for a deed (s. 201.02). Only Miami-Dade uses a different rate.

Consideration includes cash, a discharged obligation and any mortgage on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. The tax goes to the clerk when the deed is recorded. Every party to the document is liable, even when the contract says one side will pay, and if a party is exempt the other party must cover the tax.

  • Taxable: warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds, contracts for deed, and deeds in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Not taxable on the Department of Revenue's list: a personal representative's deed under a probated will.
  • Exempt: a spousal homestead deed where the only consideration is a mortgage, and divorce deeds for the marital home.

The Department also states that no specific exemption exists for transfers made for estate planning, so a family quitclaim can still carry the tax.

sections.h2: How do I find liens and judgments against a Brevard property?
sections.html:
Search the Acclaim index by party name for the owner, then search again under any prior owner and any trust or company that held title. Liens, lis pendens notices and certificates of title appear alongside deeds in the same index.

A foreclosure ends with a certificate of title issued by the clerk. After a sale the high bidder's deposit is 5 percent of the bid, and the sale stands confirmed when no objection is filed within 10 days of the certificate of sale (s. 45.031). That means a title check on a foreclosed Brevard house should show both the certificate and any surplus-fund claim the former owner filed.

If a tax certificate shows up, treat it as a timing issue. A holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the issue year, with an application fee of $75, and the tax collector must notify the titleholder, lienholders and contract-for-deed vendees before any sale (s. 197.502).

sections.h2: What can I do about private information on the public records site?
sections.html:
Brevard's Acclaim page describes two request routes created by 2021 Florida laws. One lets an affected person ask the clerk to post information about a respondent in certain minor-protection injunction cases. The other lets a person ask the clerk to remove exempt information, or images such as a military discharge or death certificate, from the website.

Removal requests must be notarized, name the statutory basis and confirm the person qualifies for the exemption. Party names generally stay in the index unless the name itself contains a street address, as a trust or company name can. If you are selling an inherited Brevard house and a death certificate sits in the public record, this is the channel to ask about.

sections.h2: Who handles the property tax side of a Brevard sale?
sections.html:
Records and taxes sit with different offices in Florida. The clerk records, the property appraiser sets value and handles exemptions, and the tax collector bills and collects (see the county organization described by the Florida Senate analysis).

On a Brevard sale, the title agent pulls the Official Records, then confirms the tax status with the Brevard County Tax Collector. The state tax calendar says unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, and the homestead exemption is lost once the owner no longer lives in the home as a permanent residence. Ask the tax collector for a current payoff figure instead of estimating one.

sections.h2: How do records work when a Brevard house comes through probate?
sections.html:
A deed from a personal representative acting under a probated will is on the Department of Revenue's not-taxable list for documentary stamp tax. The deed still has to be recorded with the Brevard clerk before the buyer's title is protected.

Florida has no estate tax for people who died after 2004, and personal representatives no longer file Form DR-312 or DR-313 (since July 1, 2023). Smaller estates may use summary administration if the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or if the owner died more than two years ago (s. 735.201). Creditors have until the later of three months after the first published notice or 30 days after being served to file claims (s. 733.702).

  • Search the owner's name under every spelling, then search the heirs.
  • Look for old mortgages that were paid but never released of record.
  • Ask the title agent to check for judgments against the heirs as well.

sections.h2: What should a seller gather before recording in Brevard County?
sections.html:
Bring the signed and witnessed deed, the parcel number, mailing addresses for the parties and the funds for recording and stamp tax. The Acclaim page links to e-recording information, so ask your title agent early whether it files that way.

Check three details before filing: names match prior records exactly, the legal description matches the last recorded deed, and each page has room for the margins the clerk requires. A rejected deed delays the closing, and the clerk's phone line, (321) 637-2004, can answer form questions.

faqs.q: Is the Brevard County recorder the same as the clerk?
faqs.a: Yes. The Brevard County Clerk of Court and Comptroller serves as the county recorder, so deeds and mortgages are filed and searched through that office.

faqs.q: Can I search Brevard Official Records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's Acclaim site offers an online search after you accept its disclaimer. Try several spellings of each name because the county gives no accuracy guarantee.

faqs.q: What does the state charge to record the first page of a deed?
faqs.a: The statutory base is $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus the trust fund and technology charges listed in s. 28.24(13). Ask the clerk for the exact total.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Brevard deed?
faqs.a: Every party to the document is liable, whichever side the contract says will pay. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk at recording.

faqs.q: Does a deed need witnesses in Florida?
faqs.a: Yes. A written conveyance of land needs two subscribing witnesses under s. 689.01, and the witnessing may use audio-video technology. Ask the clerk or a title agent to check the form before you record.
